pull.title: test: Add case for libstdc++ bug on Windows
pull.body:
The [code](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/152a55397e451fed9c10041bddf01aa6839847d5/src/wallet/migrate.cpp#L745) in `BerkeleyRODatabase::Backup()` relies on `copy_file()` with `overwrite_existing` working.

Upstream fixes:
- https://github.com/gcc-mirror/gcc/commit/017e3f89b081e4828a588a3bd27b5feacea042b7
- https://github.com/gcc-mirror/gcc/commit/35c98149a5c7af9159fa7615d8d827b3aaa3cc97
- https://github.com/gcc-mirror/gcc/commit/8b3e47b4099f319e38d357f7c646f51040a13d6e

Suggested in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36271#issuecomment-5794127014.

[Here](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin/actions/runs/39924174253/job/120344755756#step:10:1943) is an example of the failure when cross-compiling for Windows using GCC 14.2.0:
```
./test/fs_tests.cpp(145): Entering test case "copy_file_overwrite_existing"
unknown location(0): fatal error: in "fs_tests/copy_file_overwrite_existing": std::filesystem::__cxx11::filesystem_error: filesystem error: cannot copy file: File exists [C:\Users\RUNNER~1\AppData\Local\Temp\test_common bitcoin\fs_tests\copy_file_overwrite_existing\c72b38273c1f6fce4336\a] [C:\Users\RUNNER~1\AppData\Local\Temp\test_common bitcoin\fs_tests\copy_file_overwrite_existing\c72b38273c1f6fce4336\b]
./test/fs_tests.cpp(155): last checkpoint
```

A summary of reviews will appear here.
Can you elaborate on the motivation here? Why this bug specifically? Which users (compiling in what currently used  environments) do we expect to hit this?

> Can you elaborate on the motivation here? Why this bug specifically? Which users (compiling in what currently used environments) do we expect to hit this?

Even after #36042, users can hit this bug in a build environment we don’t control (e.g. a distro’s `g++-mingw-w64-ucrt64` package) that formally meets our minimum requirements but ships an affected libstdc++.
Seems harmless to add the test. An alternative could be to reject g++-mingw less than 14.3 during configure?

events.body:
> Could address the Ralph comment?

Done.

> Even after https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36042, users can hit this bug in a build environment we don’t control

Thanks:
> Why this bug specifically?"
> "Which users (compiling in what currently used environments) do we expect to hit this?" ?

It's not clear that adding a test here is that useful, unless you expect cross-compiling end-users are running the unit test binary on their systems before running bitcoind? Otherwise, as mentioned above, maybe it'd be better to reject the compiler outright.

It's also not clear what runtime failure / bug the user would be prevented from hitting (by seeing this test failure) if they happened to be using a broken compiler. If I understand correctly, does this mean that migration has likely never worked on windows with GCC-based cross-compiled binaries, but also nobody has ever reported it?

There are lots of compiler bugs, and we don't add tests for many of them, and the PR description / commit messages here don't really justify the changes, or explain how a user would be affected by this at runtime, if they used a broken compiler.
